architecturalConstraintFound.finding: Pi's shell tool execution happens inside the Pi child process itself (src/adapter/pi-rpc-adapter.mjs spawns `pi --mode rpc`); this repo's adapter code does not intercept or see individual shell commands Pi runs — it only controls whether Pi HAS tool access at all (toolPolicy: --no-tools / --tools / --exclude-tools) and what text is delivered as the prompt. The adapter's own header comment already documents this: "PI TOOL POLICY IS NOT AN OS SANDBOX ... Pi does not include a built-in sandbox."
architecturalConstraintFound.implication: A code-level call-site guard (item 2 of the Controller's Phase 0B request) cannot be wired into a shell-command dispatch point in THIS repo, because no such dispatch point exists here — Pi executes its own shell tool independently once given tool access. The only in-repo levers are: (a) the toolPolicy passed when spawning Pi, and (b) the prompt text delivered inside the task card, which IS constructed in this repo (src/v2/phase-response-contract.mjs) and IS read by Pi as its operative instruction.
architecturalConstraintFound.conclusion: Enforcement wiring for this phase targets the prompt-text lever (item 3, and effectively also closes item 2's intent within this repo's actual architecture) plus the authoritative-lookup lever (item 1). A hard OS-level sandbox around Pi's shell tool is out of VCA-1 bootstrap scope (would be a sandboxing/process-isolation project, not a bounded repair) and is not claimed as done here.

canStillBypassGuardViaArbitraryPiShellCo: Yes, in principle — Pi's shell tool is not OS-sandboxed by this codebase (documented pre-existing limitation, not introduced by VCA-1). What changed: (1) the authoritative answer to the question that triggered the original 896s grep is now a single structured read Pi is explicitly instructed to use instead, and (2) Pi's own operative prompt now explicitly forbids constructing a whole-home/root verification command and requires HOLD instead of self-widening scope. This is a strong behavioral deterrent at the instruction layer, not a hard technical guarantee — full technical prevention would require either (a) actually sandboxing Pi's shell tool (out of bounded-repair scope), or (b) never granting Pi unrestricted shell tool access for verification-only phases (a toolPolicy/graph-design question for a later phase, since toolPolicy is already a per-phase-card parameter — see src/adapter/pi-rpc-adapter.mjs toolPolicyArgs).
safeToReturnRemainingVCA1ToPiPlusAutoLoo: Yes for R1/R2 (read-only inventory/cost-reconstruction work) — those phases don't need to answer 'is anything AWAITING_EXTERNAL_REVIEW' via search (they now have currentSurfaceReviewStatus if needed) and are instructed against unbounded scans by the updated prompt. Recommend a follow-on (VCA-1 W1 or VCA-2) to evaluate restricting toolPolicy for phases that are verification-only and don't need general shell access, which would close the remaining gap technically rather than only by instruction.
